newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's foreign exchange reserves at $31.9 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's foreign exchange reserves at $31.9 bln.

text.p: South Korea's foreign exchange reserves rose to $31.9 billion at the end of May from $29.83 billion at the end of April, the central Bank of Korea said on Thursday.

The central bank attributed the increase in foreign exchange holdings to a reduction in the trade deficit, an inflow of foreign funds and subdued speculative demand for foreign currency in line with stabilisation of the won/dollar rate during May.
South Korea's customs-cleared basis trade deficit fell to $690 million in May from $1.49 billion in April.
A net of $1.16 billion flowed in during May after the foreign stock ownership ceiling was expanded to 23 percent on May 2 from previous 20 percent.
But foreign exchange reserves were off from the $33.24 billion total at the end of 1996.
